data.voice_en: When you go somewhere, the article after in gets a tag. Der Park — in den Park. Die Stadt — in die Stadt. Das Kino — ins Kino. English just says "to the" every time.
data.answer_hook_en: Answer to the riddle: a German changes the article. der becomes den. die stays die. das and in stick together into ins.

second.voice_en: The word ins is in + das in one word. People almost always say ins when going to the movies, the pool, a café: ins Kino, ins Schwimmbad.

data.bridge_en: English keeps a final d voiced: "bad" ends in a real d. German doesn't: a d at the end sounds like t. So Bad sounds like "baht", not like English "bad".
